In 1880, most of Africa was ruled by Africans.

By 1913 — 33 years later — the entire continent was European except two countries.

The fastest land grab in history — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Look at the 1880 map: European rule hugs the edges. French Algeria, British Cape Colony, Portuguese trading coasts.

Malaria, distance and African armies had kept Europe out of the interior for 400 years.

Then quinine, steamships and the Maxim gun removed all three barriers.

2/ 1884-85: Bismarck hosts the Berlin Conference. 14 powers sit around a map of Africa and set the rules for claiming it.

Not a single African was invited.

The key rule — "effective occupation" — meant paper claims were worthless. It turned colonization into a footrace.

3/ The strangest claim: the Congo, 76 times the size of Belgium, awarded to King Leopold II as his PERSONAL property.

His rubber regime worked people to death by the millions — until the scandal forced Belgium to confiscate the colony from its own king in 1908.

4/ France took the largest share — the vast Sahara and West Africa block on the 1913 map.

Britain built a near-continuous corridor from Cairo to the Cape.

Germany, Italy, Portugal and Spain carved the rest — often along ruler-straight lines drawn in European map rooms.

5/ The two survivors: Liberia, and Ethiopia — which armed itself, met Italy at Adwa in 1896, and destroyed a European army in a single morning.

Ethiopia stayed independent for another 40 years. The victory made it a symbol across the colonized world.

6/ The scramble's borders were drawn by men who had never seen the lands they divided — and most of them are still there.

That's why so many African borders run dead straight through peoples, deserts and lakes.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
